headline: CORE CPI BITES: Gold Whipsaws to $4,377, Silver Rebounds to $64.94 — Fed September Hike Still 70% Odds
snippet: August core CPI printed at 0.3% month-over-month — above the 0.2% consensus — while headline inflation held at 3.4% year-over-year, triggering a violent whipsaw in metals: gold sold off to $4,320, then snapped back to $4,377 (+1.38%), while silver recovered to $64.94 (+2.12%). Markets still price a 70% probability of a September 15-16 Federal Reserve rate hike, keeping both metals in a high-stakes holding pattern ahead of the FOMC decision.

headline: TALON METALS BEST HOLE EVER: 46.43m of 13.37% Ni + 16.54% Cu Ignites 30% Single-Day Rally at Tamarack
snippet: Talon Metals (TSX: TLO) reported the best drill result in the company's history from the Vault Zone at its Tamarack nickel-copper-cobalt project in central Minnesota: 46.43 metres grading 13.37% nickel and 16.54% copper plus cobalt, platinum-group metals and 8.6 g/t gold — pulled from 50 metres step-out of the discovery hole. Shares surged 30% on the news; Rio Tinto subsidiary Kennecott Exploration holds a 49% JV interest, giving the project significant major-company validation.

headline: SUPPLY WALL APPROACHING: Gold Demand Tops 2,500 Tonnes in H1 2026 as Annual Mine Gap Widens Past 1,300 Tonnes
snippet: Global gold demand reached 2,522 tonnes in the first half of 2026 — a record $380 billion in value — while annual mine output delivers only roughly 3,650 tonnes against demand that is pacing toward 5,000-plus tonnes for the full year, leaving a structural 1,300-tonne-plus gap plugged by recycling and above-ground stock drawdowns. With no major deposit discoveries since 2000 and permitting timelines lengthening globally, analysts warn the imbalance is accelerating and structurally floor-setting for the gold price.

headline: MONTANA MASSIVE SULFIDE OPEN AND THICKENING: American Pacific Hits 20.1m of 11.15 g/t Au at Madison
snippet: American Pacific Mining (CSE: USGD) released first assays from its 2026 drill program at the Madison Copper-Gold Project in Montana: hole M26C-02 cut 30.8 metres of massive sulfide averaging 7.4 g/t Au, 9.62 g/t Ag and 0.29% Cu, including a best interval of 20.1 metres at 11.15 g/t Au and 14.3 g/t Ag. The high-grade zone remains open to the southwest and is interpreted to be thickening in that direction — setting up step-out drilling in coming weeks to define what could be a sizeable high-grade VMS system.

headline: YEARS OF DELAYS DONE: Eldorado Gold Pours First Copper-Gold Concentrate at Skouries in Greece
snippet: Eldorado Gold (TSX: ELD) produced the first copper-gold concentrate at its Skouries project in northern Greece on September 8, marking the transition from construction to commissioning after nearly a decade of permitting delays and political opposition. The process plant now has crushing, grinding, flotation and tailings circuits running, backed by 4.6 million tonnes of stockpiled ore above reserve grade — more than seven months of feed — ahead of targeted commercial production in Q4 2026 at 140,000 oz Au and 67 million lb Cu annually.

headline: LUNDIN: U.S. Interest Payments Now Exceed Defense Spending — Gold's Bull Market Is Structural, Not Tactical
snippet: Gold Newsletter editor Brien Lundin argues in an interview with Money Metals Exchange that U.S. annual interest payments have now surpassed the entire national defense budget — a milestone that signals the debt spiral has become mathematically irreversible without monetary debasement. Lundin contends that gold investors who treat each Fed decision as the key swing factor are misreading the setup: the bull market is driven by a decades-long structural shift in fiscal credibility, not by rate-hike cycles, and dips like the current September selloff are buying opportunities within a secular trend.

headline: SMART MONEY BUYS THE SEPTEMBER DIP: Large Asset Managers Rebuild Gold Equity Positions at GDX $96-97
snippet: U.S. Global Investors' weekly Gold SWOT analysis identifies large institutional asset managers as net buyers of gold mining equities during the current September pullback, with GDX retreating 18% from its August record of $117.18 to the $96-97 range. The analysis notes that mutual funds and family offices increased allocations at this step-down level in each prior correction of the current bull cycle — and that historically, institutional re-entry at this discount to the August peak has preceded the strongest leg of the autumn seasonal rally.

headline: AUSTRALIA BREAKS GROUND: Arafura Starts $1.6B Nolans Rare Earth Mine With 1,000 Tonnes of NdPr Offtake Locked
snippet: Arafura Rare Earths (ASX: ARU) commenced construction at its $1.6 billion Nolans Rare Earths Project in Australia's Northern Territory this month, moving Australia's first fully integrated ore-to-oxide rare earth operation into execution phase with Hatch as EPCM contractor. Binding offtake agreements for 1,000 tonnes of NdPr oxide annually are now in place — 500 tonnes to Traxys North America and 500 tonnes to an Indian corporate group plus dysprosium and terbium — with practical completion targeted for late 2029 and full production of 4,440 tonnes of NdPr annually across an approximately 38-year mine life.

headline: ANTIMONY HIT 10.3% Sb AT BALD HILL: Critical Metal Discovery as China Export Controls Squeeze Western Supply
snippet: Antimony Resources Corp. (TSXV: ATMY) reported the first results from the Central Zone at its Bald Hill Antimony Project today: hole BHC-26-01 hit 2.63% Sb over 2.2 metres including a 10.3% Sb interval from 118.8 metres depth — extremely high-grade for a metal that China restricted exports of beginning in late 2023. With defence contractors and semiconductor manufacturers facing a January 2027 deadline to reduce Chinese-origin antimony sourcing, Bald Hill's discovery puts North American primary supply back on the exploration map.

headline: BRAZIL OPENS UP: GoldHaven Confirms Cu-Ni-Co and Rare Earth Settings Across 124,000-Hectare Bahia Portfolio
snippet: GoldHaven Resources (TSXV: GLDN) completed a geological reconnaissance programme across 123,900 hectares of critical minerals tenements in Brazil's Bahia and Ceará states, confirming geological settings prospective for Cu-Ni-Co and rare earth element mineralization in northern Bahia and lithium exploration targets in southern Bahia. The reconnaissance identified continuity with known mineralized belts in one of Brazil's least-explored regions; systematic geophysical surveys and channel sampling programs are now being designed for the 2026-27 field season.
